questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following:

(i) Privatisation. (2 marks)
(ii) Limited liability. (2 marks)
(iii) Deed of partnership. (2 marks)
(iv) Prospectus. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Privatisation.** Privatisation is the **transfer of ownership or control of a state-owned enterprise (public enterprise) to private individuals or firms**, for example by selling its shares to the public. Its aim is to raise efficiency and to give the government revenue.

**(ii) Limited liability.** Limited liability means that the owners (shareholders) of a company are **responsible for the debts of the business only up to the amount they have invested (the unpaid amount on their shares)**. If the company fails, their private property cannot be seized to pay its debts.

**(iii) Deed of partnership.** A deed of partnership (partnership agreement) is a **written legal document drawn up and signed by the partners** which sets out the terms of the partnership: the capital each partner contributes, how profits and losses are shared, interest on capital, salaries, the duties of each partner, how a partner may join or leave, and how disputes are settled.

**(iv) Prospectus.** A prospectus is a **document issued by a public limited company inviting the public to buy its shares or debentures**. It gives details of the company (its objects, directors, capital, past results and how to apply) so that investors can judge the risk.

questions.enonce_markdown:
"ALPHA and OMEGA" is a company created to produce animal feed. The capital raised through the sale of securities is as follows:

- 100 5% preference shares at 1000frs each,
- 50 10% debentures at 5000frs each,
- 200 ordinary shares at 2000frs each.

(i) Calculate the total capital raised through the sale of the above mentioned securities. (6 marks)

(ii) Explain THREE (3) differences between debentures and shares. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Total capital raised.** The capital raised by each security is the number sold multiplied by the price of one (the percentages 5% and 10% are the rates of return, not part of the capital raised).

| Security | Number | Price each (FCFA) | Capital raised (FCFA) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5% preference shares | 100 | 1,000 | $100\times1\,000=100\,000$ |
| 10% debentures | 50 | 5,000 | $50\times5\,000=250\,000$ |
| Ordinary shares | 200 | 2,000 | $200\times2\,000=400\,000$ |
| **Total** | | | $100\,000+250\,000+400\,000=\mathbf{750\,000}$ |

**Total capital raised = 750,000 FCFA.**

*Extra information (not asked).* The yearly fixed payments are $5\%\times100\,000=5\,000$ FCFA to preference shareholders (a dividend, paid out of profit) and $10\%\times250\,000=25\,000$ FCFA of interest to debenture holders (paid whether or not there is a profit). Ordinary shareholders receive whatever dividend is left.

**(ii) Three differences between debentures and shares.**

1. **Ownership and control.** A shareholder is a **part-owner** of the company and ordinary shareholders have voting rights at general meetings. A debenture holder is only a **creditor** (a lender to the company) and has no vote and no share in management.
2. **Return.** Shares earn a **dividend**, which is paid out of profit, varies from year to year and may be nil if the company makes no profit (a preference share has a fixed rate, but it is still paid only out of profit). Debentures earn a **fixed rate of interest**, which must be paid every year whether or not the company makes a profit, and which is an expense of the company before profit is calculated.
3. **Security and repayment.** Debentures are usually **secured on the assets of the company** and are normally *redeemable*, that is, repaid on a fixed date; in a liquidation debenture holders are paid before shareholders. Ordinary shares are permanent capital, not repaid while the company continues, and shareholders are the last to be paid, so they bear the highest risk (but also share in the high profits and in the growth of the company).
